intro: Lesson 16: The Industrial Revolution: steam, coal and factories. To understand how steam power, coal and factories changed how things were made

parts.label: Step 2
parts.text: Factories can be built anywhere with coal

questions.q: What does steam push inside an engine?
questions.model: Water boils into steam. Steam takes up more space. It pushes a piston. The piston moves the wheel.

questions.q: Who improved the steam engine in 1769?
Draw and label the steam engine cycle, then write a cause and effect chain from 'coal' to 'growing towns'.
questions.a: A labelled cycle and a logical chain of four links
questions.model: Teacher draws the first two parts of the cycle.

questions.q: Why did Britain have an Industrial Revolution first? Give two reasons.
questions.a: Plenty of coal and iron, rivers and canals, money to invest, trade

questions.q: Name one good and one bad effect of factories.
questions.a: Good: cheaper goods and jobs; bad: dangerous work and pollution

questions.q: Big question: how could boiling water change the world?
questions.a: Steam from boiling water powered machines, factories, trains and ships
